must_identify.item: The failing requests come from the pod of a separate Deployment shop-api, which shares the app=api label and is therefore an endpoint of the api Service
must_identify.evidence: Because shop-api's pod template also has app: api (plus app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api), its pod shop-api-69f6fc5964-x7m7w (10.244.1.77) got pulled into the api Service's Endpoints alongside the two legitimate api pods — 3 backends total instead of 2.

must_identify.item: That pod returns 500 because its config lacks DATABASE_URL (KeyError), while the real api pods are healthy
must_identify.evidence: DATABASE_URL is never set in the shop-api Deployment's env (only REDIS_HOST is defined), so every request routed to this pod returns 500.

notes: The primary fix is to relabel shop-api, with deletion as an alternative. Both are acceptable. Redis is mentioned only to rule it out. The optional step of adding DATABASE_URL and a separate Service is extra and does not contradict the fix.
